2026-12-26.verse: While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
theo: The day after Christmas the Church remembers St Stephen, the first martyr. It seems abrupt: from the crib to stones. But the Fathers saw the connection: yesterday Christ was born on earth so that today Stephen might be born into heaven. The Child came to give his life, and those who follow him share his self-giving.

Stephen, “full of grace and power”, sees “the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.” As he dies he prays like Jesus on the Cross: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit… Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” Among those approving his death is a young man named Saul, the future Paul. Forgiveness sown in blood bears fruit.

altar: At the Holy Qurbana we receive the Christ for whom Stephen died. Strengthened by him, we too can forgive and endure.

2026-12-26.question: Whom do I need to forgive this Christmas?

family.explain: St Stephen loved Jesus so much that he forgave the people who hurt him, just like Jesus did on the Cross.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, St Stephen saw you standing at the right hand of God. As we gather, give us his courage, his wisdom and his forgiving heart. Amen.
share: Stephen prayed: Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60). Whom do I find it hard to forgive?
Jesus says: whoever endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:22). What test of faith am I facing?
How can we support persecuted Christians?
interc: For persecuted Christians in India and throughout the world, that they may be strong and faithful.
For those who persecute Christians, that like Saul they may be converted.
For deacons, who share St Stephen's ministry.
For all who have been deeply hurt, that they may receive the grace to forgive.
For our family and parish, that we may be witnesses of Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, St Stephen prayed for his persecutors as he died. Give us his love for enemies and his courage in witness, so that we may share his crown. Amen.

illus: After the violence against Christians in Kandhamal, Odisha, in 2008, many survivors who had lost family members and homes spoke publicly of forgiving those who attacked them, and some later welcomed them back as neighbours (H). Stephen's prayer is still prayed in India.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated the birth of Christ; today we celebrate the death of St Stephen, the first martyr. It seems strange to move from the crib to the stones so quickly. But the Church wants us to understand: the Child born in Bethlehem calls for a faith that is ready to give everything.
Stephen was full of grace and power, doing great wonders and signs among the people (Acts 6:8). His enemies could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke. So they stoned him.

As he was dying, Stephen saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God (Acts 7:56). Then he prayed two prayers that echo Jesus on the Cross: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit; and, Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:59–60).

In the Gospel Jesus warns: I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves; be wise as serpents and innocent as doves. You will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:16, 22).

Stephen's greatest miracle was not his signs; it was his forgiveness. And a young man named Saul, guarding the coats of those who stoned him, would later become St Paul. Stephen's forgiveness bore fruit.

Christians are persecuted in many places today, including parts of India. Let us pray for them. And let us ask for Stephen's spirit in our ordinary lives: to forgive those who hurt us, even while the hurt is still fresh. That is the true gift of Christmas. Amen.
kids: Children, St Stephen loved Jesus so much that he forgave the people who hurt him. Can you forgive someone today?

intro: Theme: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”
St Stephen, the first martyr, the day after Christmas.

sub: Stephen sees the Son of Man at God's right hand.
Christ's birth opens heaven to us.
q: But they conspired against him, and by command of the king they stoned him to death in the court of the house of the LORD.
But filled with the Holy Spirit, he gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

sub: Jesus promised the Spirit would speak through his witnesses.
Stephen's wisdom could not be withstood.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.
For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.
points.apply: Ask the Spirit for courage to witness.

sub: Stephen commends his spirit and forgives.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter.
While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.”

concl: The crib leads to the Cross and to heaven.
Let us forgive and witness like Stephen.
